page.layout: One page of text in a single column of italic verse, with a running head at the top and the page number at the top right. No margin notes or footnotes.

p.i: Aut tuba defessas renocabat ahenea turmas: Ordine multiplici passim constructa videres Castrorum in morem niveis tentoria velis.
Scilicet ille suum populum respexit, in arctis Rebus, & infido vexatum ex hoste recepit:

Abramidas forti per mille pericula raptos Protexit clypeo Dominus, perque invia duxit- Tutus ubique fuit Iacob tanto duce, vasti Emetiens deserta soli, ceu pupula lunis Quam crystallus obit circum, & velamine multo Perspicua cingunt tunica, geminique tuentur Custodes, valuisque malum bipatentibus arcent, Quam densa pilorum acies, quam celsus obumbrat Inde superciliis mons, hinc confinia nasi, Tot munita modis tuto latet illa sub antro.

Non secus Isacidas, summi regnator Olympi Praesidio alarum occuluit, mediisque per hostes, Per loca senta, situ squallentia, duxit, ut ales Regia, quae pullos liquidas attollit in auras, Implumes audet nidos committere caelo: Ut suspensa suis paulatim librat in alis, Remigiumque docet, ducitque per aëra gyros, Certatim volitat proles aurasque lacessit Viribus impar adhuc, maternique aemula cursus: Tellurem caelumque inter gestitque pauetque, Ipsa parens oneri charo timet alma, refertque Mollibus instratis, & praeda pascit opima.
Sic Iacob tandem steriles emensus arenas

page.notes: Verse lines are set in italic throughout. Stanza breaks follow the indented lines and the sentence openings ("Scilicet", "Abramidas", "Non secus", "Sic Iacob"), which is my reading of the layout, since the indents are slight. Long s is rendered as s. The hyphen after "duxit" is a printed line-end hyphen. The spelling "renocabat" and "Isacidas" follow what I could make out, and the initial I of "Isacidas" is a best reading. Verse lines inside a stanza are separated by line breaks within one paragraph element.
